messages.author: 8954cb0a46bd963a
messages.subject: xtable
parts:
Hi D-RUGers.

I am trying to learn how to make a publication-ready table using xtable.  Here is what I have done:

> df <- data.frame(A = c(1,2,3), B = c(4,5,6))
> df
  A B
1 1 4
2 2 5
3 3 6
> print(xtable(df))
% latex table generated in R 3.1.0 by xtable 1.7-3 package
% Sat May  3 13:59:56 2014
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{rrr}
  \hline
 & A & B \\ 
  \hline
1 & 1.00 & 4.00 \\ 
  2 & 2.00 & 5.00 \\ 
  3 & 3.00 & 6.00 \\ 
   \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

It seems to generate latex code for the table.  I was surprised because the examples online show the actual table appearing at this point, but apparently there is something more I need to do with this to get the table.  I have MacTex installed on my computer, and I have used R Markdown before to knit a PDF document (in case those are involved), but it is not clear to me how to use this to generate the desired table.  If anyone could provide me with some guidance, it would be much appreciated.  

Bonnie

messages.author: 8954cb0a46bd963a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: xtable
parts:
Or, if there is a different way to make a table that is nicely formatted for publication, I would be interested in that as well.  Thanks!

Bonnie

messages.author: 2c0b1f71592389b6
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: xtable
parts:
Hi Bonnie,
Not sure if it's the correct way, but in the past I've saved the latex code generated by xtable to a small tex file, then referenced that in my master tex file with \input {path.tex}
I preferred doing it this way as if new analysis changed numbers in Table, the r code would update the small tex file that would be referenced each time master tex was compiled, rather than having to re copy paste into master.
Cheers,
Hugh.

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: xtable
parts:
Hi, Bonnie.  You might consider using one of the pandoc-related packages.  I've attached some files in which I was noodling around with the "pander" package.  Also, the "rmarkdown" package (currently available only on github or in the devel version of RStudio) has integrated a lot of pandoc stuff with knitr.  (I can send you some toy examples of this if you like, but the examples on the web are basically the same).

BTW, I assume the output format is supposed to be PDF.  You can have much more fun with HTML/CSS.

-- Mike

messages.author: 2b27719db7267c87
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: xtable
parts:
Thanks for the replies, guys!  I eventually figured out how to make the table I wanted using the package, sjPlot, which can generate a formatted table in the viewer window or browser.

# Create a table to use as example:

require(sjPlot)

sjt.df(df, describe = FALSE)

# Generates a formatted version of the table in the viewer window.

But it is also good to know about the Pander way of doing it and other options using R Markdown.  Attached is an example in which I tried the pander, knitr, and xtable ways of doing it.  I think I like pander the best, because the table comes out looking pretty nice.

Bonnie
